title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 450
paragraphs: When, however, as time went on, Periander had passed his prime and perceived within himself that he was no longer able to oversee and manage the government of the state, he sent to Corcyra and summoned Lycophron to come back and take supreme power; for in the elder of his sons he did not see the required capacity and perceived clearly that he was of dull wit. Lycophron, however, did not even deign to give an answer to the bearer of his message. Then Periander, still clinging in affection to the youth, sent to him next his own daughter, Lycophron's sister, supposing that he would yield to her persuasion more than to others'; and she arrived there and spoke to him as follows: “Brother, do you wish both that the despotism should fall to others, and that the substance of your father should be carried off as plunder, rather than that you should return and possess them? Come back home; cease tormenting yourself. Pride is a mischievous possession. Do not heal evil with evil. Many prefer what is reasonable to what is strictly just; and many before now, in seeking the things of their mother, have lost the things of their father. Despotism is an insecure thing, and many desire it; moreover, he is now an old man and past his prime. Do not give your good things to others.” She spoke to him the most persuasive things, having been instructed beforehand by her father; but he in reply said that he would never come to Corinth so long as he heard that his father was still alive. When she reported this, Periander a third time sent an envoy, saying that he himself wished to come to Corcyra, urging Lycophron at the same time to come back to Corinth and be his successor on the throne. The son having agreed to return on these terms, Periander was preparing to sail to Corcyra and his son to Corinth; but the Corcyreans, having learned all that had taken place, put the young man to death, so that Periander might not come to their land. For this reason Periander took vengeance on the Corcyreans.
